pull_requests.title: Support per-layer MTP configuration
pull_requests.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48264&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48264) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48264&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48264)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Adds independent per-layer configuration for MTP layers.

Previously, `get_mtp_config()` retained the main model's `per_layer_config`. This could apply the main-model overrides to MTP layers unintentionally.

With this PR, MTP layers discard the main model's per-layer overrides by default and can define their own through `mtp_per_layer_config`. MTP masks are created from the corresponding layer config, preserving per-layer settings such as `sliding_window`.

This also fixes MTP attention-mask selection for Inkling. Previously, mask creation looked for `layer_type` on the generic `MtpLayer` wrapper, which does not define it, and therefore always fell back to full attention. As a result, Inkling did not use the correct masks for its `hybrid` and `hybrid_sliding` MTP layers. Mask creation now selects the pattern from `layer_types` in the MTP config.

pull_requests.title: Fix MTP generation test regex gate for escaped layer ignore keys (#48003)
pull_requests.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48262&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48262) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48262&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48262)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #48003.

In `tests/generation/test_utils.py`, `GenerationTesterMixin.test_generate_with_mtp` was skipping models like `DeepSeek-V3`, `GLM4-MoE`, `GLM-MoE-DSA`, `GlmOcr`, and `HYV3` because their `_keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected` use raw regex patterns with escaped dots (e.g. `r"model\.layers\.61.*"`).

The existing skip check `re.search(r"layers\.\d+", x)` expected a literal dot immediately following `layers`, failing on strings containing `layers\.`. 

This PR updates the regex to `re.search(r"layers\\?\.\d+", x)`, allowing `test_generate_with_mtp` to run and validate all MTP-compatible models as intended.

pull_requests.title: Drop legacy MoE/MLA keys from HunYuanVL config
pull_requests.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48261&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48261) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48261&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48261)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

`tencent/HunyuanOCR` was exported from the Tencent MoE codebase, and its `config.json` still carries that codebase's routing and multi-head-latent-attention hyperparameters — at both the top level and inside `text_config`:

```json
"num_experts": 1,
"num_experts_per_tok": 1,
"moe_topk": 1,
"num_shared_experts": 1,
"use_mixed_mlp_moe": false,
"routed_scaling_factor": 1.0,
"use_mla": false,
"kv_lora_rank": 512,
...
```

HunYuanVL is a dense-only variant and declares none of these as config fields, so `PreTrainedConfig.__post_init__` falls through to its "additional attributes without default values" branch and `setattr`s every one of them onto the config. On `main`:

```python
>>> from transformers import AutoConfig
>>> config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained("tencent/HunyuanOCR")
>>> config.num_experts, config.text_config.num_experts
(1, 1)
```

That's a problem for anything downstream that sniffs the config to decide whether a checkpoint is an MoE — a dense OCR model advertises itself as a 1-expert MoE — and `save_pretrained` writes the whole group straight back out, so it propagates to every re-export.

This PR pops the legacy MoE/MLA group in `HunYuanVLTextConfig.__post_init__` and `HunYuanVLConfig.__post_init__` (the latter also sees them at the root, for the legacy "flat" checkpoint layout that `__post_init__` already handles), so they neither land on the config object nor round-trip through serialization. None of the keys are read anywhere in `modeling_hunyuan_vl.py` or `modeling_hunyuan_v1_dense.py`, so nothing else changes.

After:

```python
>>> config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained("tencent/HunyuanOCR")
>>> hasattr(config, "num_experts"), hasattr(config.text_config, "num_experts")
(False, False)
```

and a `save_pretrained` round-trip of the real checkpoint emits no MoE/MLA keys, with `hidden_size`, `num_hidden_layers` and the normalized `mrope_section` unchanged.

Added `test_legacy_moe_keys_are_dropped` alongside the existing `test_legacy_xdrope_section_normalizes_to_mrope_section`, which covers the same class of checkpoint-legacy normalization.

## Second commit: the alias half of the same problem

`HunYuanVLTextConfig`'s docstring already claimed that `pad_id`, `attention_head_dim` and `org_vocab_size` are mapped onto `pad_token_id`, `head_dim` and `vocab_size` via `attribute_map` — but only `pad_id` was actually in the map, so the other two landed as untyped duplicate attributes and were serialized alongside the canonical fields.

They are aliases, not distinct hyperparameters: no HunYuan modeling code reads either name, and `tencent/HunyuanOCR`, `tencent/Hunyuan-7B-Instruct` and `tencent/Hunyuan-A13B-Instruct` all store them with exactly the same value as the canonical field. So they're mapped rather than declared as fields.

The set of keys `HunYuanVLConfig.__post_init__` routes into `text_config` for the legacy "flat" layout now includes the text config's `attribute_map` keys too, so the aliases are normalized there instead of sticking to the root config — which also covers `pad_id`, leaking at the top level for the same reason.

Reading an alias still works (`config.text_config.attention_head_dim == 128`), it just isn't stored or serialized twice. The full `to_dict()` diff on `tencent/HunyuanOCR` is exactly the removal of `attention_head_dim`, `org_vocab_size` and `pad_id`; `head_dim`, `vocab_size` and `pad_token_id` keep their values.

- [x] Did you write any new necessary [tests](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/testing)?

pull_requests.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48259&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48259) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48259&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48259)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

`setup.py` points `transformers-mlinter` at main ahead of the `0.1.5` release. The new rules surface 30 findings; this branch takes that to 0. `make typing` and `make check-repo` pass.

⚠️ Before merge: pin setup.py back to ==0.1.5 once released (make fix-repo propagates to dependency_versions_table.py).

Findings come from three upstream changes: 

- TRF009 extended to every model file plus the public-API import form (https://github.com/huggingface/transformers-mlinter/pull/48)
- TRF038 extended to tokenization_*.py (https://github.com/huggingface/transformers-mlinter/pull/47)
- and new rule TRF058 (https://github.com/huggingface/transformers-mlinter/pull/50).

## TRF058 — 4 sites fixed

**esmfold2**: three __init__ buffers → nn.Buffer. The boundaries torch.linspace is inlined into the assignment on purpose — the modular converter reorders locals after the self.* writes that use them, which would NameError in the generated file.

**step3p7**: not an __init__ declaration but a register_buffer inside _init_weights re-materializing a non-persistent buffer Siglip already declares. Converted to init.copy_(...), matching Siglip's own _init_weights and the rotary buffers in that same method.

## TRF038 — 6 tests added, 1 bug fixed, 3 allowlisted

Five new test files (451 lines) covering 6 findings: dpr (both encoders via the mixin, plus a standalone reader class since DPRReaderTokenizer replaces __call__ with (questions, titles, texts); decode_best_spans restored from fd6bc380c8), bert_legacy (BertTokenizerLegacy and whitespace_tokenize — the parts prophetnet's tests don't reach), qwen3_5, fnet, convbert.

roberta was a bug, not a missing test. transformers.RobertaTokenizerFast tokenized character-by-character:

RobertaTokenizerFast  ->  ['T','h','i','s','i','s','a','t','e','s','t']
RobertaTokenizer      ->  ['This','Ġis','Ġa','Ġtest']

#40936 converted 13 models to XxxTokenizerFast = XxxTokenizer and missed roberta, leaving a hand-written class whose backend was never built (pre_tokenizer was None). Public and autodoc'd, but nothing in the repo imported it — hence unnoticed. AutoTokenizer never routes there, so the fix is contained: delete the module, add the alias. Docs unchanged, as with the other aliased models.

Allowlisted: bart, mobilebert, squeezebert — their tokenization_*.py define no classes at all (BartTokenizer = RobertaTokenizer), and #40936 deleted their tests deliberately. Marked in-file as a placeholder for an upstream rule change, not a permanent exemption.

## TRF009 — 6 fixed, 10 allowlisted

Six configs now resolve sibling configs through CONFIG_MAPPING with AutoConfig as the sub_configs marker, as the rule prescribes and 99 other composite configs already do: cohere_asr, esmfold2, gemma4_assistant, gemma4_unified_assistant, ovis2, sam3. Round-trips resolve the same concrete classes; 552 tests pass across the six.

Ten allowlisted, reasoning recorded in rules.toml. Two need a reviewer decision:

- generation_*.py (nemotron3_5_asr, nemotron_asr_streaming) — the rule points at modular files, but the converter has no generation_*.py support. The rule checks a file kind whose remedy doesn't exist yet.
- sam3 — AutoModel.from_config would cover the forward pass, but convert_sam3_to_hf.py:69 maps a weight to text_encoder.text_projection.weight, a key only CLIPTextModelWithProjection owns.

The rest are back-compat tokenizer shims where the import is the module's purpose. shieldgemma2 is the one genuinely fixable case left — the converter does support processing files, so it could move to a modular. Left as follow-up.
